name: str_split_1
title: Split up a string into pieces

origin.description: Split a single string into pieces and return one character vector.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: One string. A longer character vector, an empty character vector, and a missing string are errors.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Pattern to look for. The default interpretation is a regular expression. regex() sets the flags. fixed() compares literal text. coll() uses Unicode collation for a locale. boundary() matches character, word, line, and sentence boundaries. The empty string "" is equivalent to boundary("character").

origin.details: The string is checked before the split. A length-1 character vector is one string. The result is the first element of str_split(string, pattern). Every pattern rule of str_split applies, including the empty pattern as a character boundary. If pattern has length 0, the split is empty and the subscript is out of bounds. Splitting "" on "" returns character(0), because a character boundary finds no pieces.
origin.value: A character vector, the pieces of that one string.
origin.example:
fruits <- c(
  "apples and oranges and pears and bananas",
  "pineapples and mangos and guavas"
)
str_split_1(fruits[[1]], " and ")

translation.description: Split one string and return that character vector.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: One str, or a list or tuple of one str. A longer list, an empty list, and stringi._na.NA are errors.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Passed to str_split. A plain string is a regular expression. "" is a character boundary.

translation.details: The single-string check runs before str_split. A list of one string is accepted, matching a length-1 character vector. The return value is the first inner list. An empty pattern on "" returns an empty list. A pattern of length 0 makes str_split return no rows, and the subscript raises IndexError.
translation.value: A list of strings, the pieces of that one string. A missing piece is stringi._na.NA.
translation.example:
from stringr.split import str_split_1

fruits = [
    "apples and oranges and pears and bananas",
    "pineapples and mangos and guavas",
]
print(str_split_1(fruits[0], " and "))
